pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: No named regulator or licence.
Withdrawal fees the page omits.
Support channels not clearly listed.
Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
redFlags: Template placeholders left unrendered.
Return claims without verification.
The fee that is not a fee: spreads embedded in every trade.
Restriction lists that name different countries.
No verifiable company record behind the brand.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.
11 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

bottomLine: What we found is a real service wrapped in marketing that outruns its own fine print. Trade the service, not the marketing.
We rate it 4.3 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$250 minimum is the right size for testing either.
We flagged this one CAUTION because the disclosure pages leave core facts - ownership, fees and restrictions - unresolved.
